status_summary: EO 14317 (signed 2025-07-17) created Schedule G for noncareer policy-making or policy-advocating positions with no numerical cap, OPM guidance of 2025-07-29 gives the White House Presidential Personnel Office final review of placements, and OPM proposed on 2026-09-18 (91 FR 59076) to codify Schedule G in the excepted-service regulations, a rule not yet final. The Partnership for Public Service reported (report dated 2026-03-23, data through 2026-01-31) 1,835 Schedule C and 770 noncareer SES appointees, the highest Schedule C count in its historical table and 8 below the noncareer SES record, with political appointees filling 11.7 percent of filled SES positions and career SES falling from 8,127 to 5,837; Schedule G appointees were not counted. Senate-confirmed posts are the lagging part: a July 2026 Partnership analysis reported the fewest nominations of any president since Reagan and 27 confirmed officials already departed. On the SES side, a presidential memorandum of 2025-01-20 directed agencies to reconstitute Performance Review Boards and to have senior noncareer officials chair and form a majority of Executive Resources Boards, and OPM memos of 2025-02-04 (chief information officer posts) and 2025-02-24 (all career-reserved posts) asked agencies to request redesignation of career-reserved SES positions as general, with requests due 2025-03-24; a May 2026 CRS report describes these steps as ones that would lead to some redesignations but gives no count, and no list of approved redesignations was found. A government-wide civilian hiring freeze ordered on 2025-01-20 was followed by EO 14356 (2025-10-15), which requires agency strategic hiring committees to approve career vacancies, broader than the Mandate's freeze on top career hiring, and exempts noncareer SES, Schedule C and Schedule G positions. Separately, an OPM final rule effective 2026-03-09 (91 FR 5580) lets agencies place policy-influencing career positions in Schedule Policy/Career, which keeps them career but at-will. The White House Cabinet page (modified 2026-10-01) does not list the OPM Director.

timeline.event: A presidential memorandum froze hiring of federal civilian employees government-wide, with exceptions including national security and public safety; Senate-confirmed presidential appointments, noncareer SES and Schedule C appointments were excluded from the freeze (extension tracked in c06-10).

A presidential memorandum on career senior executives (90 FR 8481, published 2025-01-30) directs agencies to end existing Executive Resources Boards and form new ones chaired by, and with a majority of, senior noncareer officials alongside career members, and to reconstitute Performance Review Boards with members committed to enforcing SES evaluations.
OPM asks agencies to request redesignation of career-reserved chief information officer SES positions as general so that noncareer appointees may fill them (as described by CRS).

OPM's Acting Director asks agencies to review career-reserved SES positions and, by 2025-03-24, submit a revised list and requests to redesignate the rest as general, starting with posts at deputy assistant secretary level and above; the memo notes a statutory floor of 3,571 career-reserved positions and says the count has grown to about double that.

EO 14317 (90 FR 34753, published 2025-07-23) creates Schedule G in the excepted service for noncareer positions of a policy-making or policy-advocating character that normally change with a presidential transition, including positions whose appointment needs White House Presidential Personnel Office assent; no numerical cap in the order, and Civil Service Rules on removal do not apply except as statute requires.
OPM issues Schedule G guidance: agencies coordinate through OPM's Executive and Schedule C System, and final review and approval rests with the White House Office of Presidential Personnel.

OPM SES rule published (effective 2025-10-15); OPM may exclude noncareer SES members from forced distribution, and Performance Review Board language shifts from diversity to commitment to the appraisal system. It does not address career-reserved positions or PRB composition.

EO 14356 requires strategic hiring committees (deputy agency head, chief of staff and designees) to approve each vacancy filled or created, plus annual staffing plans; noncareer SES, Schedule C and Schedule G positions are excluded from its limits.

OPM publishes the final rule (91 FR 5580, RIN 3206-AO80, effective 2026-03-09) allowing agencies to move career positions of a confidential or policy-influencing character into Schedule Policy/Career, whose incumbents remain career employees but are at-will and outside adverse action procedures and appeals (tracked in c03-01).

OPM publishes a proposed rule (91 FR 59076, RIN 3206-AO92) that would add Schedule G to the excepted-service regulations at new 5 CFR 213.3701 and treat it like Schedule C for several purposes (exclusion from performance-based removal procedures, counting as political appointments, SES conversion rules), and would revise Schedule Policy/Career at 5 CFR 213.3601; comments are due 2026-11-17 and the rule is not final.

title: Staff political appointee ranks and limit career control of policy positions
uncertainties: Appointee counts come from one nonprofit report (data through 2026-01-31) and a secondary article; a second article dated 2026-04-27 gives the Schedule C count as of the end of 2025, so the exact count date differs by source. No official OPM count of Schedule G placements was found. The statement that political appointees exceed any past share of SES is the Partnership report's characterization. The Cabinet-page finding reflects one page read on 2026-10-07 and does not show whether the OPM Director attends Cabinet meetings. OPM memos of 2025-02-04 and 2025-02-24 sought redesignation of career-reserved SES positions as general, and CRS (R48932, 2026-05-01) says these steps would result in some redesignations, but no count of approved redesignations was found; the latest Federal Register list of career-reserved positions found covers calendar year 2024 (published 2025-05-20). Whether reconstituted Executive Resources Boards are in fact chaired by noncareer officials at each agency was not checked. Not re-checked: the 2025 Senate rule change on en bloc confirmations (tracked in c01-03). The stage is implemented because the core mechanisms (Schedule G, record noncareer appointments, White House approval of placements, noncareer-led Executive Resources Boards) are operative, while the Senate-confirmed cadre, Cabinet status and completed career-reserved redesignations are not shown. EO 14317 (90 FR 34753) and the proposed rule (91 FR 59076) were read on federalregister.gov in this review, the proposed rule except roughly its last 15,000 characters; no effective date appears in the part read. The Schedule Policy/Career final rule (91 FR 5580) was read in part (first 100,000 of about 118,000 characters), so its position estimate and any litigation notes were not confirmed; that rule keeps covered positions career, so it is context rather than an increase in political posts. The Partnership for Public Service and Government Executive reports, CRS R48932 and the Cabinet page are kept as sources rather than timeline events because they are publications or page checks, not government actions.
